closure_conditions.V5_note: 0.08% is LUCK, NOT MARGIN. This is the single number on which the corrected chain is thinnest, and it is stated as such rather than reported as comfortable.

constants_that_FAILED_to_recompute.what: the coefficient inside the reduced M_4^U
constants_that_FAILED_to_recompute.failing_clause_location: arXiv:2509.25116v2 LaTeX e-print main.tex line 2242; the printed 2.8e-6 appears in the reduced form at lines 2247-2248, character-exact '- 2.8 \times 10^{- 6} \times M_3^U'
constants_that_FAILED_to_recompute.why_harmless: 4 eps^U = 4 x 6.5e-7 = 2.6e-6 exactly. The paper writes 2.8e-6, which is LARGER, so the subtracted term is LARGER and M_4^U comes out SMALLER than the truth. The error is in the safe direction, and the next step does not use it: it uses the certified bound 0.002.

constants_that_FAILED_to_recompute.diagnosis: eta_2 = 0.005 has been substituted where M_2^U <= 0.0061 belongs. eta_2 is declared at main.tex line 2255 as 'where $\eta_2 = 0.005$ is the $L^2$ coefficient of $E$-norm in \eqref{eq:eig M}.' and M_2^U is certified at main.tex lines 2270-2271 as <= 0.0061. The two are different objects that happen to look alike; the smaller one was used, making the denominator LARGER and x_0^U SMALLER than the truth.
constants_that_FAILED_to_recompute.why_not: carried through the whole chain, every downstream closure condition still holds.

conservative_mismatches_recorded_but_not.what: the paper's prefactor drops the -M_2^U term

independently_re_derived_by_V5: the Bogovskii tail scaling int_{|x|>R}|x|^{-p} dx = 4 pi R^{3-p}/(p-3)
the heat-smoothing/similarity exponent cancellation, giving t^{1/2 - 3/(2p)} independent of k and r
alpha = 1/4 and (p-3)/(2p) = 1/8 = alpha/2, with delta ~ 0.0565 < delta_1 = 1/8

localisation_step.the_load_bearing_strictness: The L^s L^q claim's inequality 3/q + 2/s > 1 is STRICT and that strictness is load-bearing: at equality the time integral diverges logarithmically. The paper claims only the strict side, and uses it correctly.

sign_convention_resolved.apparent_problem: the printed eigenvalue lambda-bar ~ -0.113 looks stable
sign_convention_resolved.resolution_verbatim: We remark that we flip a sign of the linearized operator in the second equation of \eqref{eq:NS eq eig} due to the convenience of elliptic estimates.
sign_convention_resolved.consequence: the eigenvalue of L_Utilde is -lambda-bar ~ +0.113 > 0, i.e. UNSTABLE, as the argument requires.

CLAUSE_2.NOT_FOLDED_INTO_CLAUSE_1: This verdict was reached from measurements of the shipped data alone and does not depend on, and is not conditioned on, the clause-1 answer.
CLAUSE_2.meaning: The certified profile IS genuinely 3D. W2's predicate FAILS on all three conjuncts.

W2_test_located_in_the_record.predicate: a certified profile is a 2D LIFT iff (L1) no dependence on one Cartesian coordinate (N_x3 = 0, extent 1) AND (L2) u^(3) == 0 AND (L3) omega^(1) == omega^(2) == 0 with only omega^(3) nonzero. Genuinely 3D iff the conjunction FAILS.
W2_test_located_in_the_record.note: W2's test was located in the record and used as the arbiter. Nothing was invented.

CLAUSE_2.rule_R2c_pre_committed_before_reading: axisymmetric WITH OR WITHOUT swirl counts as 3D under W2's test, because W2's test is about the LIFT STRUCTURE, not about the number of independent variables. This rule was frozen in PART 0 SS0.2.1 BEFORE the paper was opened, so that the axisymmetry the paper advertises could not be used to bend the verdict either way.

the_certified_object_tied_to_shipped_dat.how_the_tie_was_established: up_eig.mat's stored lambda = 0.1131420327438595 matches the paper's printed eigenvalue -0.11314203274385938 to SIXTEEN significant figures. The shipped data IS the certified object, not a lookalike.
component_identification_cross_confirmed: the SS4.6 Y/X/Z vector-spherical-harmonic basis mode counts (Y has M modes, X has M+1, Z is the free swirl family) -- u2 has shape 301 x 150 = M+1, confirming the X family
set_div_free! updates only u2, which is correct precisely because for axisymmetric flow div u involves only u_r and u_theta, leaving u_phi free

predicate_applied_conjunct_by_conjunct.conjunct: L1 -- no dependence on one Cartesian coordinate (extent 1)
predicate_applied_conjunct_by_conjunct.why: theta-mode extent is 150, not 1; 45000 of 45150 coefficients are nonzero
the swirl u_phi has max|u_phi| = 8.754198315291823, which is 57% of max|u_r|. This is not a numerical residue; it is a principal component of the profile.

predicate_applied_conjunct_by_conjunct.conjunct: L3 -- omega^(1) == omega^(2) == 0, only omega^(3) nonzero
predicate_applied_conjunct_by_conjunct.why: nonzero swirl with theta-dependence generates poloidal vorticity; the meridional components do not vanish

CLAUSE_2.contrast_with_the_failure_mode_this_clau: Wave 2 measured that two certified rows in arXiv:1902.00384 were 2D LIFTS: Vishik's unstable vortices are steady states of the 2D EULER equations, lifted to 3D axisymmetric vortex rings WITHOUT SWIRL. That is exactly the construction whose u^(3) vanishes identically. THIS paper's profile carries swirl at 57% of the radial component, so it is NOT that construction. The paper's own sentence describing the lifted case, character-exact at main.tex lines 98-99, is 'that are steady states of the 2D Euler equations, and lifted them to 3D axisymmetric vortex rings.'
CLAUSE_2.axisymmetry_flagged_but_NOT_WEIGHED: The paper states at main.tex line 2509 'We consider the axisymmetric case throughout the computations and denote the cylindrical coordinates as $(\rho,z,\phi)$.' and at line 2192 'leveraging axissymmetry and parities' (the misspelling is the authors'). Under pre-committed rule R2-c this observation does NOT bear on the verdict and was not allowed to.
CLAUSE_2.consequence_per_pre_committed_reading_b: Reading (b) pre-committed that a NO here would be the MORE CONSEQUENTIAL answer, and a W2 finding rather than a W3 one. The answer is YES, so that branch is NOT taken: there is no 2D lift in the Grade-A x fluid cell on this paper's account, and W2 gains nothing here.
